tables.title: Test-Set Performance
notes: Trained on 112 cases, tested on 38 held-out cases (25%, seed 123).
The no-information rate is the accuracy of always predicting the largest class.

tables.title: Variable Importance
notes: Permutation importance: loss of test accuracy when the predictor is shuffled.

assumptions.message: Training and test accuracy are close.

interpretation.text: A naive Bayes classifier predicting species from 4 predictors classified 94.7% of 38 held-out cases correctly (95% CI [82.3, 99.4]; κ = 0.92), compared with 36.8% for always predicting the largest class. The most important predictor was petal_length.

title: Naive Bayes
code:
library(ggnext)
# Naive Bayes (classification): species ~ sepal_length + sepal_width + petal_length + petal_width
predictors <- c("sepal_length", "sepal_width", "petal_length", "petal_width")
d <- data[complete.cases(data[, c("species", predictors)]), c("species", predictors), drop = FALSE]
d$species <- droplevels(factor(d$species))
d$species <- droplevels(d$species)
# Hold out 25% of the cases to test the model
set.seed(123)
test_rows <- sample(nrow(d), round(0.25 * nrow(d)))
train <- d[-test_rows, , drop = FALSE]
test <- d[test_rows, , drop = FALSE]
fit <- e1071::naiveBayes(species ~ ., data = train, laplace = 0)
predict_fn <- function(newdata) predict(fit, newdata, type = "raw")
# Performance on the held-out test set
classes <- levels(train$species)
prob <- predict_fn(test)
pred <- factor(colnames(prob)[apply(prob, 1, which.max)], levels = classes)
confusion <- table(Predicted = pred, Actual = test$species)
n_test <- sum(confusion)
accuracy <- c(sum(diag(confusion)) / n_test, binom.test(sum(diag(confusion)), n_test)$conf.int)
chance <- sum(rowSums(confusion) * colSums(confusion)) / n_test^2
kappa <- (accuracy[1] - chance) / (1 - chance)
no_information_rate <- max(colSums(confusion)) / n_test
by_class <- data.frame(class = classes, sensitivity = diag(confusion) / colSums(confusion),
                       specificity = (n_test - rowSums(confusion) - colSums(confusion) + diag(confusion)) / (n_test - colSums(confusion)),
                       precision = diag(confusion) / rowSums(confusion))
by_class$f1 <- 2 * by_class$precision * by_class$sensitivity / (by_class$precision + by_class$sensitivity)
train_accuracy <- mean(colnames(prob)[apply(predict_fn(train), 1, which.max)] == train$species)
# Permutation importance: loss of test accuracy when one predictor is shuffled (mean of 10 shuffles)
score <- function(data) mean(colnames(prob)[apply(predict_fn(data), 1, which.max)] == data$species)
set.seed(123)
importance <- sapply(predictors, function(v) mean(replicate(10, {
  shuffled <- test
  shuffled[[v]] <- sample(shuffled[[v]])
  score(test) - score(shuffled)
})))
importance <- sort(importance, decreasing = TRUE)
importance_df <- data.frame(variable = names(importance), importance = as.numeric(importance))[seq_len(min(length(importance), 20)), ]
importance_df$variable <- factor(importance_df$variable, levels = rev(importance_df$variable))
# Names are drawn inside the panel, left of the data (ggnext clips long axis labels)
label_pad <- min(0.5, (max(nchar(as.character(importance_df$variable))) * 7 + 12) / 500)
importance_df$label_x <- min(0, importance_df$importance) - (max(importance_df$importance) - min(0, importance_df$importance)) * label_pad / (1 - label_pad)
p_importance <- ggnext(importance_df, aes(importance, variable)) +
  geom_importance() +
  geom_text(aes(x = label_x, y = variable, label = variable), anchor = "start") +
  labs(title = "Variable importance", x = "Importance") +
  theme(axis_title_y = FALSE, axis_text_y = FALSE, base = theme_modern())
confusion_df <- data.frame(predicted = pred, actual = test$species)
p_performance <- ggnext(confusion_df, aes(predicted, actual)) +
  geom_confusion_matrix() +
  labs(title = "Confusion matrix (test set)", x = "Predicted", y = "Actual") +
  theme_modern()
p_performance <- p_performance + labs(color = "Share of actual")
